### Linked conditional model

The model starts at 31 March 2026 and carries cash, debt, working capital, fixed capital and share counts through monthly pre-entry intervals and every month after entry. Base growth 8%, EBITDA margin 12%, D&A8% of revenue, total capex 8%, receivable/inventory/payable days 300/110/170 and other net capital 25% of revenue are **repair assumptions**, not achieved economics. The bear combines−5% growth,3% EBITDA margin, slower collections/inventory and shortened supplier funding. The upside uses 20% growth,22% EBITDA margin,6% D&A and materially better collections. Working-capital repair is phased over a year rather than credited instantly.

A cash month first pays capex, working-capital deployment, legacy taxes and principal, then credits operating receipts after new taxes and interest. Every intermediate event must retain the ₹1 crore required operating buffer. Falling below it invalidates the ordinary return, even if cash remains above zero; this is a conservative model requirement, not evidence of an actual default. Demand-related-party debt ₹3.8691 crore is paid first and other debt over the first year, explicitly conservative analytical timing because contractual maturity evidence is missing. Legacy dues ₹2.334953 crore are paid over three months; they are not deducted twice. Cash already received on warrants is embedded in the March anchor, never added again. No new borrowing, rollover or optional equity is treated as committed.

Counterfactual rescue is clearly separate: issue at 50% of the candidate entry price,2% fees, minimal whole shares, at most ₹10 crore gross, no more than 20% of starting shares and no more than authorized headroom **after reserving 902,780 warrant shares**. The headroom cap is 839,597 rescue shares. Rescue may occur before entry only as an explicit counterfactual, not a reconstruction of actual shares or actual funding. If this cap is exhausted or terminal reinvestment is unfunded, terminal common equity and return are null. Ordinary paths never retain a terminal return after an earlier cash failure.

### Earned terminal valuation and intrinsic cross-check

Terminal enterprise value is not an arbitrary peer multiple. It is derived from next-year NOPAT, terminal growth and return on incremental capital:

`EV = next NOPAT × (1 − terminal growth / terminal ROIC) / (WACC − terminal growth)`.

Terminal growth 2/3/4%, ROIC10/13/18% and WACC18/16/14% correspond to bear/base/upside assumptions. Growth remains below WACC. Any capital needed to support terminal NOPAT above the modeled committed-capital proxy is a separate terminal cash event, subject to the same buffer and bounded whole-share rescue rules. The annual cash tables precede that separate terminal event; the final equity bridge uses post-event cash and shares. Debt and the operating cash floor are deducted; only excess available cash is added; the associate receives no separate speculative value. Issued plus actual model rescue/conversion shares form the per-share denominator. No dividends are counted while retaining the same cash.

For optional-financing paths, the DCF remains an operating enterprise-value diagnostic; undiluted investor per-share DCF values are withheld. Diluted terminal-wealth returns control the shareholder outcome. The conditional intrinsic cross-check discounts the explicit future FCFF plus earned terminal operating value, then bridges from enterprise to entry equity. It does **not** add terminal retained cash after already discounting FCFF. All DCF values, terminal shares of value, earned multiples and detailed rows are included in the canonical model. Where funding fails, intrinsic equity and return conclusions are suppressed. Investor annualization uses dated five-year endpoints with 1% entry and 1% exit cost assumptions, before personal tax. Costs 0% and 3% are tested because an observed spread was unavailable.
